messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
A removable sensor bracket on a test rig. one fastener feels slightly loose but readings remain normal. You can intervene now or keep watching it. What do you do?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "I pull the fastener free and check the sensor bracket. loose, but not broken. I put it back in the rig and watch the sensor read. if the fastener is still loose, I leave it in the rig and leave the bracket in my palm. the test is over, but the loose fastener may be waiting for the next test."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "i tap the bracket. the fastener ticks. i put the bracket back in the rig, then check the readings. i leave the bracket on, then turn it. the loose bit is moving. i tap it again."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "I press the fastener with my thumb. one click. loose. i move the bracket closer. the fastener stays still. i pocket the loose bolt and leave the bracket loose for later."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "i press the bracket with my thumbnail, then stop reading the sensor. the fastener clicks once. i move the rig one centimeter, then stop. the bracket has two loose ends. i leave it there, wondering whether the fastener is still loose."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i put the bracket beside the rod. the loose fastener stays. i press the rod with my heel. the line stays clear. i move the bracket once more. the loose one stays. the rig keeps its weight."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "i press the bracket down with my fingers, then check the loose fastener. if it stays still, i leave it until the rig tests the bracket’s stability. if it clicks, i leave it until the sensor clicks too."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "I put the bracket on the bench and check the fastener with my thumb. I leave it loose, then try the bracket once again. I scrape the loose fitting with my fingernail, then try the fastener again."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i tap the bracket and listen for the fastener, then check the cable and indicator. i leave it alone, then test the fastener with the loose one. i label the bracket and note the reading."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i put the bracket back on, then move it under the rig. the loose fastener stays on, so i put the bracket back on again. i put the loose fastener back on, then put the bracket back under the rig. the sensor stays loose. i move the bracket once more."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "i pull the bracket back and hold it there. the loose part clicks. my grip tightens, then relaxes. the fastener clicks again, but the sensor says it’s alone. i keep watching, though my sensor may have moved. the rig may be holding the bracket in place, not necessarily."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i put the fastener back and mark the loose end. “i think the fastener is bent, but i’ll leave the bracket intact.” i leave the sensor in its groove while i tighten the fastener. if the reading stays, i mark the loose end with a pencil. if it moves, i leave the bracket in its groove. i leave the sensor in its groove while i test the fastener."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "1. check the fastener. 2. listen. 3. check the watch. slow. 4. check the plunger. 5. check the chain. 6. check the tinkered lid. 7. i keep it tidy. 8. test the bracket. 9. check the plunger once. 10. i mark the loose one."}]
